answer_1.quote: Neural dialogue generation has drawn increasing attention due to its vast commercial values and practical demands... we propose a novel model to handle this new type of training data consisting of {implicit scenario, response} pairs.

answer_2.quote: We employ two kinds of automatic metrics to evaluate all models. The reference-based metrics, perplexity (PPL), BLEU (%), and the embedding metrics (including embedding average (AVE), embedding greedy (GRE), embedding extrema (EXT)), and coherence (COH) ... The count-based metrics, distinct (Dist-{1,2,3} (%)) and KL divergence, are used to evaluate the lexical diversity and the distribution distance of the responses.

answer_4.quote: We conducted human evaluation to assess the quality of response. We randomly selected 200 test examples from each dataset and asked three annotators to judge which generated response in each pair (RegDG and baseline) is better (i.e., win, lose or tie) in terms of Diversity, Relevance, and Fluency.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were asked to compare each pair of responses and indicate which one wins, loses, or ties for each of the three criteria: Diversity, Relevance, and Fluency.
